Subject: Sharp p99 increase + answer coherence drop after INT8 rollout

Neha —

We rolled the INT8 profile you provided into our inference pool this morning (canary -> 50%). Since ~15:00 PDT we've observed:

- P99 latency jumped from ~420ms to ~1.1s for large prompts (60-150 tokens).
- Error spikes: transient 5xx for some sessions (appears request-level timeouts).
- Output coherence: customers report hallucinations on multi-turn prompts that previously were fine (examples attached).

I attached a small sample of user prompts + server traces (cedarhill_p99_traces.zip). This is impacting a live feature (mortgage pre-fill) and our ops team wants a rollback unless we have a fast mitigation.

Can Redwood help immediately? We need:
1) Quick root cause triage (are we seeing kernel issues with INT8 on your runtime?)
2) Recommended rollback or knob to limit the new profile across our Dedicated pool
3) Exec-level ETA for resolution so we can decide on rollback

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

—Aaron

Subject: Re: Sharp p99 increase + answer coherence drop after INT8 rollout

Neha / Karthik / Aaron — quick preliminary from runtime team after ingesting traces:

- We see decode-time amplification on requests with long context + many attention heads. INT8 kernels on the customer's GPU family (A2x) show a regression in the fused attention path for sequence lengths >96. That manifests as token decode stalls and higher P99.
- There's also an interaction with prefix KV caching: when a prefix is reused across many sessions, the quantized KV cache is ~18% larger in memory which causes more cache churn on nodes with tight memory accounting, leading to request-level timeouts (5xx).
- Regarding coherence/hallucination: we observed a small but consistent drop in softmax numerical stability on some sequences post-quantization (rounding noise). For multi-turn prompts with narrow-context disambiguation, that can push logits enough to create rare hallucinations.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered by impact / time-to-execute):
1) Roll the routing for Cedar Hill dedicated pool back to FP16 profile (Karthik can flip routing flag). Expected immediate effect: P99 back to baseline within the hour.
2) If rollback is not acceptable, apply a temporary decode-time cap (max_tokens per call) to avoid long-sequence stalls; reduces throughput but avoids 5xx.
3) Engineering follow-up: recompile INT8 kernels with stable accumulation path and adjust rounding strategy (requires runtime release, ~3-5 days) + new quant calibration on Cedar Hill's prompt set to improve coherence.

I'll attach a short artifact "runtime_int8_trace_notes.txt" to the internal thread and open a ticket to prioritize the kernel fix.

—Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
